text: When he started again. <break time="0.8s" /> The dog did not want to leave the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> For it knew that it was far too cold to travel. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, at a place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the snow looked perfectly solid. <break time="0.8s" /> The man broke through and wet himself halfway to the knees. <break time="0.8s" /> He was angry at his luck. <break time="0.8s" /> Because he now had to build a fire at once. <break time="0.8s" /> And dry his socks and moccasins. <break time="0.8s" /> He built the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Under a large spruce tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Pulling twigs from the bushes. <break time="0.8s" /> And adding bigger branches. <break time="0.8s" /> As the flame grew. <break time="0.8s" /> The old timer had said that no man should travel alone. <break time="0.8s" /> In the Klondike after fifty below. <break time="0.8s" /> But here he was alone and safe. <break time="0.8s" /> He smiled and thought that some of those old timers. <break time="0.8s" /> Were much too careful about the cold. <break time="0.8s" /> But each time he pulled a twig. <break time="0.8s" /> He shook the tree a little. <break time="0.8s" /> And the heavy snow on its boughs. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to move. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a great mass of snow fell. <break time="0.8s" /> Without warning. <break time="0.8s" /> On the man and the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> And the fire was blotted out. <break time="0.8s" /> It was as though he had just heard. <break time="0.8s" /> His own sentence of death. <break time="0.8s" /> And for a moment. <break time="0.8s" /> He sat and stared at the spot. <break time="0.8s" /> If he had had a trail mate. <break time="0.8s" /> He would have been in no danger now. <break time="0.8s" /> For his partner could have built the fire.
